country.name: North Macedonia
country.tagline: The Vardar valley's sun-soaked Vranec, the ruins of Stobi and the Balkans' biggest winery at Kavadarci.

stats.note: Vineyard: State Statistical Office via FAOSTAT (official figure), 21,534 ha in 2024; Wein.plus gave 24,776 ha of wine vineyards in 2022. Production: 854,000 hl in 2022 (Wein.plus); GIZ (2026) expected 90 to 100 million litres in 2025, at least 85 percent exported

country.overview:
North Macedonia is a wine exporter first: in a normal year it makes 0.9 to 1 million hl and sends at least 85 percent abroad, much of it in bulk to Serbia, Croatia, Germany and beyond. In the 1980s it made about two-thirds of Yugoslavia's wine. The vineyard (about 25,000 ha for wine, plus large plantings of table grapes) is dominated by red grapes, about 80 percent, and above all by Vranec, with roughly 9,500 ha. Smederevka (Dimyat) is the main white.

Three regions organise the country: Povardarie, the Vardar valley from Skopje to the Greek border, with about 85 to 87 percent of vineyards and 90 percent of wineries; Pčinja-Osogovo in the east toward Bulgaria; and Pelagonija-Polog in the west, including Ohrid and Prespa. The heart of Povardarie is Tikveš, the basin around Kavadarci and Negotino, where hot summers (often over 35 °C), Mediterranean air funnelled up the Vardar from the Aegean and cold continental winters give dark, ripe, full-bodied reds. Tikveš winery in Kavadarci, which dates its history to 1885, is the largest in South-Eastern Europe; Stobi, Bovin, Popova Kula, Chateau Kamnik and Dalvina lead the newer estates.

Native grapes include Stanušina, a light, local red of Tikveš, and Kratošija (Tribidrag/Zinfandel). The ancient city of Stobi on the Vardar, with mosaics showing vines and wine, recalls that Paeonians, Macedonians and Romans all made wine here. Since 2024 amendments to the Wine Law have aimed to introduce EU-style geographical indications, and the first, 'Vardar Valley', was being prepared in 2026.

history.title: Stobi on the Vardar
history.text: Stobi, a Paeonian then Macedonian and Roman city at the confluence of the Crna and Vardar, has mosaics with vine and wine motifs; the Stobi winery nearby takes its name.

history.title: Tikveš winery
history.text: Tikveš winery in Kavadarci dates its founding to 1885; it became a cooperative after 1946 and was privatised with new investment in 2003. It is described as the largest winery in South-Eastern Europe.

history.title: Yugoslavia's vineyard
history.text: Macedonia produced about two-thirds of Yugoslav wine; output fell from about 1.8 million hl in the mid-1990s to 447,000 hl in 2002 after the federation broke up.

history.title: Toward geographical indications
history.text: Wine Law amendments in 2024 opened the way for EU-style GIs; 'Vardar Valley' was being prepared as the first, coordinated by the Povardarski wine region body.

country.classification: North Macedonia has three wine regions (Povardarie, Pčinja-Osogovo, Pelagonija-Polog) subdivided into 16 to 18 wine areas (*vinogorja*) such as Tikveš, Skopje, Veles, Ovče Pole, Gevgelija-Valandovo, Strumica-Radoviš, Kočani-Vinica, Kratovo, Kumanovo, Prilep, Bitola, Ohrid, Prespa, Tetovo and Kičevo. Labels have long used 'controlled origin' wording tied to these areas. Wine Law amendments adopted in April 2024 set up an EU-compatible system of geographical indications; as of early 2026 the first GI, 'Vardar Valley', was in preparation. Note that the EU PGI 'Macedonia' refers to Greek Macedonia.
country.climate_soils: The Vardar valley is a corridor of hot, dry summers and Mediterranean influence from the Aegean, with cold winters and frequent wind; soils are alluvial, sandy and clay-loam on terraces, with limestone and schist on the hills. The west (Ohrid, Prespa, Bitola) is higher and cooler.

grapes.name: Vranec
grapes.note: About 9,500 ha: the national red, dark and tannic, from rustic bulk wine to aged single-vineyard bottlings.

grapes.name: Smederevka
grapes.note: About 6,500 ha, the main white (Dimyat elsewhere).

grapes.name: Stanušina
grapes.note: Rare native red of Tikveš, light and fragrant.

grapes.name: Temjanika and Žilavka
grapes.note: Aromatic Muscat and Herzegovinian white grown in smaller amounts.

further_reading: Wines of Macedonia (Tikveš, Stobi producer sites)

regions.name: Povardarie
regions.tagline: The Vardar valley and Tikveš: hot, sunny, Vranec-dominated and home to nearly all the wineries.
regions.summary: Povardarie, the Vardar river valley, holds about 85 to 87 percent of the country's vineyards and 90 percent of its wineries. Its subregions include Skopje, Veles, Ovče Pole, Tikveš, Gevgelija-Valandovo and Strumica-Radoviš. Tikveš, around Kavadarci, Negotino and Demir Kapija, is the most famous, with Tikveš winery, Stobi, Bovin, Popova Kula and many smaller estates.
regions.history: Stobi's Roman ruins and Tikveš's 19th-century winery mark the long continuity of wine here.
regions.terroir: Alluvial terraces and clay-loam hills; hot dry summers, cold winters, Aegean influence.
regions.grapes: Vranec, Kratošija, Stanušina, Smederevka, Temjanika, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Chardonnay.
regions.styles: Ripe, dark reds; fresh whites; bulk wine for export.
regions.classification: Wine region with 8 subregions; first GI 'Vardar Valley' in preparation (2026).

sources.title: GIZ: Macedonian wine will receive a geographical indication (Feb 2026)

regions.name: Pčinja-Osogovo
regions.tagline: The eastern hills toward Bulgaria: Kratovo, Kočani and Kumanovo.
regions.summary: Pčinja-Osogovo covers the eastern hills along the Pčinja river and the Osogovo mountains toward Bulgaria, with subregions such as Kočani, Kratovo, Kumanovo and Pijanec. It is cooler and higher than the Vardar valley and makes fresher wines.
regions.history: Kratovo sits in the crater of an extinct volcano and has a long winemaking tradition.
regions.terroir: Volcanic and metamorphic soils, continental climate.

sources.title: GIZ: Macedonian wine will receive a geographical indication (Feb 2026)

regions.name: Pelagonija-Polog
regions.tagline: The high west: Bitola, Prilep, Ohrid and Prespa.
regions.summary: Pelagonija-Polog spans the west, from the Pelagonia plain around Bitola and Prilep to Ohrid and Prespa lakes and Tetovo and Kičevo in the Polog valley. Higher altitudes and lake influence give fresher, lighter wines.
regions.history: Ohrid's monasteries and Bitola's Roman Heraclea Lyncestis recall a long wine history.
regions.terroir: Lake and mountain influence, cooler climate; alluvial and limestone soils.
regions.grapes: Vranec, Smederevka, Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir.

sources.title: GIZ: Macedonian wine will receive a geographical indication (Feb 2026)

mk-tikves.name: Tikveš
mk-tikves.grapes: Vranec, Kratošija, Stanušina, Smederevka, Temjanika, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay
mk-tikves.summary: Tikveš is the country's most famous wine area, a sun-baked basin in the middle Vardar valley around Kavadarci, Negotino and Demir Kapija. It holds the largest share of the vineyard and the Tikveš winery (founded in 1885), whose Barovo and Bela Voda single-vineyard reds, developed with consultant Philippe Cambie, showed what the area's Vranec, Kratošija and Plavac can do. Stanušina is the local red.

sites.name: Tikveš winery, Kavadarci
sites.text: Tikveš winery in Kavadarci dates its founding to 1885. It became a cooperative after 1946, was privatised with new owners in 2003, and calls itself the largest winery in South-Eastern Europe. Its Barovo and Bela Voda single-vineyard reds are named after Tikveš localities.

sites.name: Stobi archaeological site
sites.text: The ruins of Stobi, a Paeonian, Macedonian and Roman city at the confluence of the Crna and Vardar rivers, include mosaics with vines and drinking scenes. They are a reminder that the Vardar valley has made wine for well over two thousand years.

sites.name: Stobi winery
sites.text: Founded in the 2000s near Gradsko and named after the nearby Roman city, Stobi is one of the most modern wineries in the Vardar valley. It makes Vranec, Žilavka, Temjanika and Bordeaux varieties.

sites.name: Popova Kula, Demir Kapija
sites.text: Popova Kula, on a hill above Demir Kapija ('iron gate') where the Vardar cuts through a gorge, is a winery and guesthouse that has championed the local red Stanušina.
